sentences.text: 3. In the FIR, it was alleged that on 7.12.2023 there was suspicious trade on proprietary account of Bhansali Value Creations Private Limited.
The said fact was brought to the notice of Relationship Manager of Bombay Stock Exchange Limited (BSE) and request was made to block the trade.
The Relationship Manager informed the western region head of BSE about illegal trade.
The region head contacted All India Marketing head of BSE who informed that trade can be cancelled within 30 minutes from trade.
Since the time has lapsed, complaint will have to be filed with police.
The company lodged preliminary complaint.
It was learnt that the authorised dealer of complainant company Mr. Meet Rajput unauthorisedly entered company trading terminals.
Mr. Meet Rajput was introduced by the petitioner.
He executed the illegal trade.

4. On 7.12.2023, some trades were executed in SENSEX23D1571500PE on the platform of respondent No. 4- BSE Limited, wherein one of the counter-parties is respondent No. 2- Bhansali Value Creations Private Limited and the petitioner is the other counter-party.

After the execution of the aforesaid trade and in the usual course, the petitioner would have received the payment from respondent No. 3 once respondent No. 3 had received it from respondent No. 6.
6.

However, the payout at present is being withheld pursuant to the direction dated 7.12.2023 from Cyber Police Station, Pune (Respondent No. 1) issued to respondent No. 4 on account of FIR No.
263 of 2023 lodged with Pune City Cyber Police Station by respondent No. 2 and so, it has not been made to respondent No. 3.

Respondent No. 4, in turn, informed the clearing corporations i.e. Indian Clearing Corporation Limited and NSE Clearing Limited (Respondent Nos. 5 & 6 respectively) about the Police's direction dated 7.12.2023, who have withheld the payout.

Out of the total payout retained by respondent Nos. 5 and 6 in terms of the aforesaid direction received from Cyber Police Station, Pune (Respondent No. 1), a sum of Rs. 4,22,68,240/- is attributable to the trade executed by the petitioner.

This amount is retained by respondent No. 6.
7.

The petitioner had approached respondent no. 2 to settle the dispute amicably and they have agreed to an in-principle settlement whereby the petitioner has given an unconditional and unequivocal discharge from all claims to respondent Nos. 2 to 6 and has agreed that he has no claim on the said amount of Rs. 4,22,68,240/- ("said amount").
4-WP-692-24.odt 8.

2 respondent No. 1 be returned to respondent No. 2.

sentences.text:
Memorandum of Settlement of Disputes was made on 17.1.2024 between Bhansali Value Creations Private Limited (respondent No.2), Jenish P. Padariya (petitioner) and Nikhil J.
Kathairiya.
In the Memorandum of Settlement of Disputes, it is stated that Jenish (petitioner) and Nikhil are in judicial custody in FIR No.263 of 2023.
They are expecting to receive a payout for the trades they have made in SENSEX23D1571500PE on 7.12.2023 from Fyers Securities Private Limited.
On the other hand, Fyers Securities Private Limited (respondent No.3) is waiting to receive the payout from BSE Ltd.
The payout has been stopped and secured with BSE Ltd., NSE Clearing Ltd and India Clearing Corporation Ltd..

Banhsali Value Creations Private Limited has filed application before Bombay High Court under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act seeking interim relief against Fyers Securities Private Limited (respondent No.3), Jenish (petitioner), Nikhil, BSE Ltd. (respondent No.4) and NSE Clearing Limited (respondent No.6) and the same is registered as Commercial Arbitration Petition.
Jenish (petitioner) and Nikhil approached respondent No.2- Bhansali Value Creations Private Limited to settle disputes.

Jenish (petitioner) and Nikhil agreed that they relinquish all 4-WP-692-24.odt their rights, title and interest in the payout amount which is receivable by them from respondent No.3 -Fyers Securities and/ or respondent No.4-BSE Ltd. for trades executed on 7.12.2023.
They further agree to discharge and release respondent No.2- Bhansali, respondent No.3-Fyers, respondent No.4-BSE Ltd and any other person from any and all claims demands, actions suits, damages.
They undertake to file affidavits before Arbitral Tribunal or Bombay High Court.

10. The respondent No.2 has filed consent affidavit stating that on 7.12.2023, some trades were executed in SENSEX23D1571500PE wherein one of the counter parties is respondent No.2 and petitioner is other counter party.

The petitioner is expecting to receive a payout from BSE Ltd.
(respondent No.4).

The payout at present has been stopped and secured with respondent No.4-BSE Ltd., respondent No.6 - NSE Clearing Ltd. and respondent No.5 Indian Clearing Corporation Limited on account of proceedings in FIR No. 263 of 2023.
The petitioner had approached respondent No.3- Bhansali to settle the disputes amicably and the parties have agreed to an in principle settlement.

The respondent No.2 states that prayer (b) and (c) seeks to bring on record the settlement terms between petitioner and respondent No.2 and petitioner has discharged all other respondents and requested that money withheld be returned to respondent No.2.
The total principal amount receivable by petitioner from the said trade is Rs.4,23,57,428 out of withheld amount.

The petitioner has consented that respondent No.6-NSE Clearing 4-WP-692-24.odt Limited/respondent No. 4-BSE Limited may be directed to disburse the said amount to respondent No.2 - Bhansali Value Creations Private Limited.
The amount of Rs.4,23,57,428 with accrued interest be disbursed to respondent No.2.
the respondent No.2 consents to quash the FIR qua the petitioner.
11. The respondent No. 6 is not a party to the FIR.
The role of respondent No. 6 was limited to withholding the payout payable to respondent No. 3 pursuant to the e-mail dated 7.12.2023 from respondent No. 4 to respondent No. 6.

Learned Advocate for respondent No.6 submitted that the respondent No.6 has not signed consent terms and in the event the directions are issued the respondent No.6 would release the subject amount to respondent No.3.

The petitioner and all the other respondents have no objection for releasing amount to respondent No.2 as agreed by the Jenish Pravinbhai Padariya vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76529680/

sentences.text: It is agreed that pursuant to the directions of this Court, the withheld payout be released by respondent No. 6 to respondent No. 3 and in turn from respondent No. 3 to the petitioner.
The same shall be done by respondent No. 6 within three days from uploading the order.
Pursuant to the payout being released to the respondent No. 3, the respondent No. 3 shall transfer the same to the petitioner within three days thereafter.
The said monies have not been kept in a fixed deposit and were retained in a current non interest bearing account.
12. Upon the receipt of funds from respondent No. 3, the petitioner agrees to transfer the said sum so received to 4-WP-692-24.odt respondent No. 2 within a period of 3 days.
All related proceedings between the petitioner and the respondents shall be withdrawn.

13. In view of the settlement arrived at between the petitioner and the respondent No. 2, we pass the following orders:
a. Respondent No. 6 is directed to pay to respondent No. 3 the sum of Rs.
4,22,68,240/- within a period of three days from the date of uploading this order.
b. Once the respondent No. 3 receives the sum of Rs. 4,22,68,240/-, it shall transfer the same to the petitioner within three days thereafter.
Upon receiving such sum, the petitioner shall transfer the said sum to respondent No. 2 within a period of three days of such receipt.

c. The petition is allowed in terms of prayer clause (a) and FIR No. 263 of 2023 dated 14.12.2023 registered with Pune City Cyber Police Station under Sections 120-B, 34,
408, 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Sections 43-A, 66 and 66 (D) of the Information Technology act, 2000, the charge-sheeting bearing No. 2 of 2024 and the entire proceedings in RCC No. 691 of 2024 pending before the 6th Joint Civil Judge Junior Division and Judicial Magistrate First Class, Pune
are hereby quashed insofar as they relate to the petitioner after the petitioner has transferred the sum of 4-WP-692-24.odt Rs.4,22,68,240/- to respondent No. 2 as stipulated hereinabove.
d. The undertakings of the petitioner contained in the Memorandum of Settlement of Disputes dated 17.01.2024 (Exhibit B to the petition) are accepted as undertaking given to the Court.
14. It is made clear that the present petition has been allowed on account of the settlement arrived at between the petitioner and respondent No. 2.

Separately, respondent No. 2 has also consented to quash the FIR No. 263 of 2023 and the charge-sheet bearing No. 2 of 2024 and the entire proceedings in RCC No. 691 of 2024 pending before the 6th Joint Civil Judge Junior Division and Judicial Magistrate First Class, Pune against the petitioner (the Respondent No. 3 herein) in Criminal Writ Petition (st) No. 4522 of 2024.
